1: This ship has no means of generating energy. It could end up stranded and unable to move if its batteries are depleted.
2: This ship's energy supply is not sufficient to run the thrusters at full power. Its top speed and acceleration will be diminished.
3: This ship's energy supply is not sufficient to run the steering at full power. Its turn rate will be diminished.
4: This ship's energy supply is not sufficient to run both thrusters and steering at the same time. Its movement will be diminished.
5: This ship is powered entirely by solar energy. It could be difficult to maneuver if you fly too far from the center of a star system, because your engines will only have a fraction of the power they require.
6: This ship consumes fuel, but has insufficient storage. If it took off, it would immediately run out of fuel.
7: This ship has no hyperdrive. If it took off, it would be unable to leave this star system.
8: This ship has insufficient fuel capacity to make a hyperspace jump. If it took off, it would be unable to leave this star system.
9: There are insufficient bays available to carry this ship. If it took off, it would be unable to leave this star system.
10: This ship has insufficient energy storage to fire an installed weapon. Install outfits that increase your energy storage, or if you have no energy storage, ensure that your "surge" energy is greater than the firing energy per shot of your weapons.
11: Governments that scan for illegal goods will attack you upon discovering this item in your possession in space, or arrest you if found when landed.
15: Turn your flagship opposite its current direction of flight. If reverse thrusters are installed, accelerate backwards.
17: Fire your flagship's afterburner, if one is installed.
18: If the "Automatic aiming" setting is off, activate automatic aiming when this key is held.
19: Land on the selected planet. If no planet is selected, automatically selects a planet to land on, or attempts to land on the planet you are directly on top of if traveling at low speeds. If a planet is already selected, double tapping will cycle to the next planet.
20: Initiate a hyperspace jump to follow your current travel plan. If you have no travel plan, initiates a jump nearest to your current facing angle. When held, commands your escorts to get ready to jump and only initiates the jump when released.
21: With <shift>, your fleet will not jump until every ship in the fleet is ready for every system in the travel plan instead of needing to hold the key at each system.
25: With <shift>, select the nearest ship regardless of hostility.
26: Select the next non-escort ship in the system, cycling through all ships.
28: Hail the selected ship or planet. If both a ship and planet are selected, hails the ship.
30: Board the selected ship. If no boardable ship is selected, selects a ship to board based on the "Boarding target priority" setting.
31: With <shift>, selects an escort to board.
32: Select the nearest asteroid based on the "Target asteroid based on" setting.
33: Scan the selected ship, if you have outfit or cargo scanners installed.
34: Fire all of your flagship's primary weapons. The "automatic firing" setting will fire only those weapons that are within your target's range.
35: Toggle the "Turret tracking" setting between "focused" and "opportunistic". See the "Turret tracking" setting tooltip on the Settings tab for more details.
